quotes.where: Script row 0:02-0:05, narration (also beats.md, 30-second video row 0:02-0:05)
quotes.quote: On Mars, nobody comes to get you.
quotes.why_generic: A movie-trailer slogan. Any Mars survival entry in this challenge could open with it, and it spends 3 of 30 seconds without a number or a place.
quotes.rewrite: She is 913 metres from the habitat. Walking back costs 54 grams of oxygen.

quotes.where: Script row 0:20-0:30, narration, last sentence (also beats.md, same row)
quotes.why_generic: The video closes on a slogan, which the rubric bans. Any team with a credits page can say it, and it shows no count.
quotes.rewrite: We checked our terrain against NASA Mars Trek at 564,001 points. The typical difference is 14 centimetres.

quotes.where: Script row 0:20-0:30, narration (also beats.md, same row)
quotes.quote: Next: EVA planners rehearse a walk before they fly it, and students plan one with the same NASA data.
quotes.why_generic: Professionals plus students is the audience line of every Space Apps entry. No planner has used it, and nobody flies a walk.
quotes.rewrite: Next: a heart rate sensor sets the oxygen use, and the same pipeline loads any site with a HiRISE terrain model.

quotes.where: Script row 0:20-0:30, on-screen text (also beats.md, same row)
quotes.quote: For EVA planners and classrooms · free in the browser
quotes.why_generic: Every web hackathon project is free in the browser and for classrooms. It names nothing this app does.
quotes.rewrite: 0.14 m RMS vs NASA Mars Trek · 564,001 points · martian-map.fernando-haro-c.workers.dev

quotes.why_generic: Fits unchanged on the data slide of every team in the hackathon. The headline under it already does the work.
Product-brochure label, one step from the banned 'immersive'. It says how it should feel, not what the four panels are.
quotes.rewrite: ONE EVA: PLAN, WALK, REACT, REVIEW

quotes.quote: Who uses it, and what we build next.
quotes.why_generic: The stock last-slide headline of any pitch deck. It also makes the deck end on a roadmap, while the rubric asks for a hard fact.
quotes.rewrite: 0.14 m from NASA Mars Trek, at 564,001 points. (Move the Mars Trek check here as the headline, keep heart rate and any HiRISE site below it.)

quotes.quote: plan a Mars walk with open NASA data, in a browser
quotes.why_generic: 'Open NASA data, in a browser' describes every Space Apps web entry. No school, grade or lesson is named.
quotes.rewrite: plan the 930 m route to Cheyava Falls and see whether the margin stays above the 30 min reserve (or cut the card)

quotes.quote: rehearse a walk on real terrain before they fly it
quotes.why_generic: An untested user claim any simulator team makes. 'Real terrain' is an adjective where the deck has a number, and 'fly' is wrong for a walk.
quotes.rewrite: compare three route profiles (fastest, gentlest, radio) on the 1 m HiRISE model before approving one

quotes.where: Slide 7, caption under the QR code
quotes.why_generic: True of most entries. It wastes the one line a judge reads before scanning.
quotes.rewrite: Scan to walk the 55 m first sortie

quotes.why_generic: Template section label, as is 'THE IDEA' on slide 3. Both come with the deck template of any team.
quotes.rewrite: CHEYAVA FALLS, JEZERO CRATER (slide 2) and THE MARGIN (slide 3)

quotes.where: Demo lines, D1 (script-5min-es.md D1: 'Todo es Jezero, con datos de la NASA.')
quotes.quote: All of this is Jezero, from NASA data.
quotes.why_generic: 'From NASA data' with no instrument is the superficial-addition phrasing the Relevance criterion marks down. Beat 5 names the missions two minutes later.
quotes.rewrite: The mission table. This is 1.5 km of Jezero from the HiRISE model, one metre per pixel.

quotes.where: Demo lines, D2 (script-5min-es.md D2: 'Cada capa dice qué decide.')
quotes.quote: Each layer says what it decides.
quotes.why_generic: Abstract and hard to parse by ear. A judge with no context cannot tell what a layer deciding means.
quotes.rewrite: cut. Start at 'Terrain: the HiRISE slope. The route goes around yellow and never crosses red.'

quotes.where: Optional opening, row 0:00 (script-5min-es.md: 'Volvimos. Refritos, nueva generación.'; beats.md beat 0 on screen: 'Refried. New generation.')
quotes.why_generic: 'We're back' is a sequel tagline, and 'new generation' sits next to the banned 'next-generation'. It delays the cold open the rules ask for.
quotes.rewrite: cut the tagline. Keep 'first of seventeen in Ensenada, Global Nominees' and go to Jezero.

quotes.why_generic: An announcement that says nothing, and a forced group of three. The rubric says to give the number and the source and stop.
quotes.rewrite: cut. Start with 'A real heart rate sensor driving oxygen use, through NASA's model (Hoffmann 2021).'

quotes.where: Question 12, EN (ES: 'corre en el navegador, sin instalar nada')
quotes.quote: Users: EVA planners rehearsing a walk, and classrooms, since it runs in a browser with nothing to install.
quotes.why_generic: The standard who-would-use-it answer of any browser project. No planner or teacher has tried it, and a judge will ask.
quotes.rewrite: Nobody outside the team has used it yet. The first test is a class in Ensenada planning the 930 m route to Cheyava Falls. (Team to confirm.)

quotes.where: Question 8, EN, first two sentences (ES: 'El mapa es el producto. La simulación es la prueba')
quotes.quote: The map is the product. The simulation is the test
quotes.why_generic: Paired aphorism in the 'X is the Y' mould. It sounds rehearsed and puts the real answer one sentence later.
quotes.rewrite: The same HiRISE map runs in three places: the mission table, the visor minimap and the wrist. Walking it with 771 g of oxygen is how we test that it reads in a glance.

quotes.where: Question 8, EN, last sentence (ES: 'Todo lo que no pone información en el mapa o actúa sobre ella lo dejamos fuera.')
quotes.quote: Anything that doesn't put information on the map or act on it stayed out.
quotes.why_generic: A design-principle claim a judge cannot check, and one any team can make. The app has an AI start video and a partner astronaut that test it.
quotes.rewrite: cut, or name what was dropped.

quotes.where: Beat 2, The rules, first sentence (script-5min-es.md: 'Las reglas son de la NASA.'; slide 2: 'NASA rules')
quotes.why_generic: Borderline. The sentence is a slogan on its own, and the three numbers after it carry the beat. It costs a second and names no document.
quotes.rewrite: Three limits, from NASA's xEVA plan and Apollo 17.

overall: The local 5-minute script and slides 1, 3 and 6 are clean and specific, with no banned word anywhere, and the slop sits in the 30-second video (a slogan at each end and a generic audience line), slide 7, the template kickers and the who-uses-it answers.
